title: Guidelines for Efficient Construction of Diatom Episomes Using Gibson Assembly
author: Jernej Turnšek
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jy7cpzn

steps.title: Set up PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the desired expression cassette (e.g., using the NR promoter/terminator) with appropriate primers; avoid using a plasmid template that carries Amp or Tet resistance genes to reduce risk of template carry‑over.

substeps.instruction: Select template DNA without Amp or Tet resistance (or be prepared for gel purification).
Prepare PCR mix according to standard conditions.

steps.title: Gel‑extract PCR product
steps.instruction: Run the entire PCR reaction on an agarose gel, excise the correct band, and purify the DNA; this eliminates template plasmid carry‑over and removes the need for DpnI treatment.

substeps.instruction: Load the whole PCR reaction onto a gel.
Run electrophoresis until separation is clear.
Excise the band of expected size.
Purify the DNA using a gel‑extraction kit.

steps.title: Perform Gibson Assembly
steps.instruction: Combine the purified PCR fragment with the other Gibson parts (e.g., a 4‑piece assembly) using the Gibson Assembly master mix and incubate according to the kit instructions to generate the diatom episome.

substeps.instruction: Mix all fragments in the appropriate molar ratios.
Incubate at the recommended temperature and time.

steps.title: Transform and plate cells
steps.instruction: Transform the Gibson Assembly product into competent E. coli and plate on fresh Amp100 LB agar plates or, preferably, carbenicillin‑supplemented plates to minimize satellite colonies; alternatively, disrupt the Tet resistance gene to avoid satellite colonies.

substeps.instruction: Perform heat‑shock or electroporation with the assembly mix.
Plate on Amp100 LB agar or carbenicillin plates.

steps.title: Screen colonies by PCR
steps.instruction: Screen transformants using colony PCR with OneTaq 2× Master Mix (Standard Buffer), running a 12.5 µL reaction (instead of the usual 25 µL minimum) to verify correct assembly.

substeps.instruction: Pick individual colonies into PCR tubes.
Set up 12.5 µL PCR reactions with OneTaq 2× Master Mix.
Run PCR under appropriate cycling conditions.
